title: Day 1: USE YOUR GIFTS
description:
One of the greatest qualities of being a Christian is offering living support and kindness to each other and our friends.

**1 Pet 4:9-11 "Offer hospitality to one another without grumbling. Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God's grace in its various forms. If anyone speaks, they should do so as one who speaks the very words of God. If anyone serves, they should do so with the strength God provides, so that in all things God may be praised through Jesus Christ. To him be the glory and the power for ever and ever. Amen."**

Peter requests that each of us should identify our gifts and use that individual gift to serve and benefit one another. One may have the gift of caring for the sick at home or in hospitals. Others maybe good at serving, cleaning and organizing food for events. Still others may show their warmth and love in close and caring fellowship. Some are very sincere to pray for the needs of others and they are prompt even to check how we are doing.

All gifts that are developed by the Holy Spirit within us who makes us feel willing and interested to come forward to serve even without having to be called forward, it's so natural. Peter says in V11, all these gifts that are used by each other will be praised that they see the same spirit and imitation of Christ in us.

In **Roman 7:6,** Paul writes that this is the NEW WAY in the Holy Spirit which was not done when we just followed the law without any actions.

**Practical Action**

Each of us have a special set of skills that can be beneficial for the church. Find a time and opportunity when you could volunteer so your spiritual gifts could help build up the church.

title: Day 2: SERVING OTHERS IN GOD'S WILL
description:
**_Ephesians 6:6-8 <sup>6</sup> Do not be servants by eye-service, as men-pleasers, but as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart. <sup>7</sup> Be a slave, not a slave, but a free man, knowing that each one will receive his reward from the Lord for whatever good he does. <sup>8</sup> Do not be pleasing men, but with good will serving the Lord._**

I have built many relationships in my life with wealth, money, and my own selfish actions and I have to please them no matter what they want whether right or wrong, regardless of the consequences. For this, I have made many efforts in my life, and there was no truth in it many times.

I have done everything to please others, to feel proud. But this has led to many failures, the consequences of my mistakes which led to more regrets. But when I choose to be a servant of Jesus Christ, I am able to love people and build a relationship that is genuine. Then I am able to see their pain, their suffering through the true love of Christ and then build a strong and true relationship.

**In John 12:26 Jesus says, whoever serves me must follow me. We have to learn from Jesus ways about the ways we treat others.** Our heavenly father will honour the one who serves others. Therefore love sincerely, bear with the weaknesses of others.

**Practical Actions:**

Build genuine relationships just as Jesus was a great servant to his friends. Find out the needs others have in their life and pray for them.

title: Day 3: CARRYING EACH OTHER'S BURDENS
description:
**Galatians 6:2 "Bear one another's burdens, and thus fulfil the oath of Christ."**

Many people in today's world are smiling on the outside but are carrying heavy burdens on the inside. Some struggle with family issues, some with financial difficulties, some with heartbreak. God wants to use us as instruments of love to such people.

**Christ's desire Is to be** Loving one another, helping the needy, being forgiving and compassionate and to show selfless service

**By bearing one another's burdens,** we fulfil Christ's command of love by sharing in the sufferings and needs of others. As Jesus bore the burden of our sin on the cross, we must show His love to the world when we share in the burdens of others.

- Whom can I comfort today?
- Does my love and actions reflect the love of Christ?

**Practice Actions:**

Try to find who are all in pain around you. Pray for them and pray with someone in particular today. Ask God to give them strength to carry their pain and challenges.

title: Day 4: BEING CAREFUL SERVANT
description:
**1 John 3: 17-18 _17 If anyone has material possessions and sees a brother or sister in need but has no pity on them, how can the love of God be in that person? 18 Dear children, let us not love with words or speech but with actions and in truth._** If a man has worldly goods, and finds his brother lacking, and closes his heart to him, how will the love of God be revealed in him? Let us not love with just words of encouragement, but also with actions as a sign of service. John's desire in this verse is not just to show pity when you come across disciples who struggle, but to find a solution (even if it material need) to immediately benefit the person. No matter how much property, money, or jewelry we have, if we do not have the spirit of helping others, God's love will not be in us. When our hearts are hardened not to help others, we do not stay with God. We only see the faults of others, but God sees us with love every day. We are called to show the same love and support to others.
**Practical Actions: **Can you give a small gift of love to a disciple in your ministry or church who are in need?

title: Day 5: PRACTICES OF CHRIST IN THE MINISTRY
description:
**Romans 14:17-18 _17 For the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit. 18 He who serves Christ in these things is loved by God and approved by men._**
In these verses, Paul teaches us that true service in God's kingdom is marked by righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit. Righteousness in service means choosing to do what is right before God, even when our efforts go unnoticed by others. It is serving with sincerity, integrity, and a heart that seeks God's approval above human praise in everything you do. . Peaceful service focuses on building unity and strengthening relationships. Rather than insisting on our own preferences or methods, we seek what helps others grow and draws them closer to God. Joy in the Holy Spirit enables us to serve with gratitude and gladness instead of obligation. When we recognize that we are participating in God's work, service becomes a privilege rather than a burden. The Holy Spirit fills us with the strength and joy needed to continue serving faithfully. When our service reflects righteousness, peace, and joy, people see the character of Christ through our lives. This is one of the greatest ways we can serve both inside and outside the church. By living and serving in this manner, we help others experience God's love, grow closer to Him, and become part of His mission in the world. Such service not only honors God but also leaves an eternal impact on the lives of those around us. ** Practical Actions:** See every work you do as a service to God. Thank God for every opportunity he provides you to serve Him and others as well

title: Day 6: EXCELLENCE IN SERVICE
description:
**  
Matthew 23:11 "The greatest among you shall be your servant. "**

Who is an "employee"?  
The Greek word used here for an employee is diakonos. It refers to the servants who serve out of love and without compulsion. The world says. "Get up. "Jesus said. "Get down - there is real greatness. "  
Jesus has been a great example for this greatness. He washed his disciples' feet (John 13:5). He didn't come to make others work for Him but to work for others (Mark 10:45). Greatness in the kingdom of God is not about how many people serve you, but how many you serve.  
As we serve, it is important to examine our motives. Are we seeking recognition and appreciation from others? Do we serve only when it fits our schedule or benefits us? Are we willing to help only those with whom we are comfortable? Jesus teaches that genuine service is not driven by personal gain, pride, or the desire for praise. Instead, it flows from a heart that loves God and cares for people. True servants quietly meet needs, encourage the discouraged, take initiative to help without being asked, and choose humility over recognition. Their focus is not on being noticed, but on reflecting Christ through selfless acts of love.

**Practical action  
**In your home, in the Church, or in the neighborhood find a way to serve someone today.

title: Day 7: BEAR ONE ANOTHER
description:
**Ephesians 2:10 "_For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them."_**

**We are God's Workmanship**

A master sculptor does not carve a stone aimlessly; behind it lies a grand purpose to chisel a masterpiece. In the same way, God has saved us and transformed us into a new creation in Christ with a clear purpose. That purpose is "good works."

We did not come into this world by mere chance. God has designed you and me like a masterpiece. Do you know why? Not for us to sit idle, but to do good to this world-a path He planned and prepared for us beforehand.

**Romans 15:1** **"_We then who are strong ought to bear with the scruples of the weak, and not to please ourselves."_**

**The Purpose of Strength is to Bear the Weak**

V:1 beautifully explains what that "good work" given to us in Ephesians 2:10 actually means.

The spiritual strength, knowledge, talents, or resources that God has blessed us with are not meant for us to live just to please ourselves but to uphold and "bear the weak" who are stumbling either in their faith or in their lives.

**Practical Action:**

Pray for three people whom you think is weak in their faith. Meet with at least one of them to help them draw strength from God.

title: Day 8: BECOME A GIVER NOT A TAKER
description:
**Ephesians 4:28 "Anyone who has been stealing must steal no longer, but must work, doing something useful with their own hands, that they may have something to share with those in need"**

reminds us that God calls His people to live with honesty, diligence, and generosity. While we often hear about major crimes in the news, there are many smaller forms of dishonesty that can quietly become part of everyday work life. Since we spend a large portion of our lives at work, our workplace becomes one of the most important places where our faith is tested and displayed.

In many work environments, people may be tempted to cut corners, misuse resources, exaggerate results, or seek personal advantage at the expense of integrity. The world often encourages us to do whatever it takes to get ahead, making dishonesty seem acceptable or even necessary for success. As followers of Christ, however, we are called to a higher standard. Our work is not merely a way to earn money but an opportunity to honor God through faithful and ethical living.

Paul teaches that becoming a Christian involves a complete transformation. We are to leave behind our old patterns of selfishness and dishonesty and embrace a new way of life that reflects Christ. Our faith should shape how we work, how we treat others, and how we handle responsibilities. There is no separation between our spiritual life and our work life; both belong to God.

True repentance begins when you stop asking, "What can I receive?" and start asking, "What can I give?"

**Practical:**

Pray for your forgiveness if you have been cheating anyone financially. And give a thought to where can you be giving?

title: Day 9: DON'T BE FIRST
description:
**Mark 9:33-35 _"Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all."_**

We often admire those who have influence, recognition, authority, or success. We measure greatness by titles, achievements, followers, income, or the respect we receive from others. It is easy to bring this same mindset into our relationships and even into the church, seeking positions that make us feel important or wanting our efforts to be noticed and appreciated.

Jesus turned this way of thinking upside down. He taught that greatness in God's kingdom is not about being first, but about being willing to serve. Kingdom greatness is seen in humility, selflessness, and a willingness to put the needs of others before our own.

Serving one another is often expressed through ordinary, everyday actions. It may be patiently caring for a family member after a long day, helping a co-worker without expecting credit, listening attentively to a friend, or quietly meeting a need that others overlook. These acts may never receive public recognition, but they matter deeply to God. In a world that celebrates visibility and status, Jesus calls us to a life of faithful and humble service.

When we choose to serve rather than seek recognition, we reflect the heart of Christ. Every act of love, kindness, and sacrifice becomes an opportunity to build others up and draw them closer to God. The true greatness in God's kingdom is not climbing above others, but stooping down to serve them.

Take a few moments to examine your own life:

- How much does the desire for recognition influence your decisions?
- Are you willing to do tasks that receive little or no appreciation?

**Practical Actions:**

Pray for the person you think is poorest or in difficult conditions to be lifted up. Is there anything you can do for them

title: Day 10: SERVICE REVEALS YOUR HUMILITY
description:
**Philippians 2:3-4 _Do nothing out of envy or malice, but in humility consider one another better than yourself. Look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.  
_**

**1 Peter 4:9 _Treat each other without grudges._**

Philippians 2:3-4 teaches us to do nothing out of selfish ambition but to value others above ourselves and look to their interests as well as our own. Similarly, 1 Peter 4:9 calls us to show hospitality without grumbling. Together, these passages remind us that Christian service is rooted in humility and love.

When we think about humility, we often assume that pride is its greatest enemy. However, if we look deeper, selfishness is often what keeps us from serving others wholeheartedly. We naturally think about our own comfort, preferences, time, and needs before considering those of others. Yet God calls us to a different way of living. Instead of being self-centered, we are called to reflect the character of Christ by putting others first.

Jesus is the perfect example of this. Though He is God, He willingly took the nature of a servant and humbled Himself for the sake of others. His life was marked by sacrificial love, compassion, and service. As His followers, we are called to imitate that same attitude. Serving others is not merely a responsibility; it is an opportunity to display the heart of Christ.

**Practical action:  
**whom do you find hard to show your humility? What does it say about you? What effort can you make today to grow in Humility of Christ?

title: Day 11: GIVING IS A BLESSING THAN RECEIVING
description:
**Acts 20:34-35** **"_In all this I have given you an example that by such work we must support the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus, for he himself said, 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"_**

Paul's words reveal an important principle of the Christian life: believers are called to use their resources, abilities, and opportunities to strengthen those who are weak. The weak may be those who are struggling financially, emotionally, spiritually, or physically. Rather than ignoring their needs, followers of Christ are called to support and encourage them.

Paul then recalls a saying of Jesus: "It is more blessed to give than to receive." Although this statement is not recorded in the Gospels, it was preserved in the teaching of the early church. Jesus taught that true blessing is found not in accumulating possessions or receiving benefits, but in generously giving to others. The world often measures success by what a person gains, but God's kingdom measures success by what a person gives.

Giving is not limited to money. We can give our time, encouragement, compassion, prayers, wisdom, and practical help. Every act of generosity reflects the character of God, who freely gives grace, mercy, and love to his people. When we give selflessly, we participate in God's work and become channels of blessing to others.

**Practical Actions:**

Look for one person today who needs encouragement and intentionally reach out to them. Share your time, resources, or abilities with someone who has a genuine need.

title: Day 12: DON'T GET TIRED TO BE GOOD
description:
**Galatians 6:9-10** **_"Let us not become weary in doing good, for if we do not give up, we will reap in due time. Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people, especially to those who belong to the family of believers._**

Doing good sounds simple, but it is not always easy. There are times when helping others feels exhausting. At times, even our acts of kindness go unnoticed, unappreciated, or even misunderstood. In those moments, discouragement can creep into our hearts.

That is why Paul encourages believers not to grow weary in doing good. God knows that serving others faithfully requires perseverance. The strength to continue does not come from ourselves but from the Lord. When we feel tired, He renews us. When we feel discouraged, He reminds us that our labor is never in vain.

Every loving act, every word of encouragement, every prayer offered on behalf of another person is precious in God's sight. He sees what others may overlook. God's promise is that in His perfect timing, we will reap a harvest if we do not give up. The results may not be immediate, but God is always at work through our faithfulness.

Today, let us take advantage of every opportunity God gives us to do good. As we do, may our lives become a living testimony of the love, grace, and compassion of Jesus.

**Practical Actions:  
**Repeat this prayer several times today, Lord give me strength not to be weary in doing good. Help me to show love and compassion to all those I meet today. Let my life be a manifestation of your glory.

title: Day 13: SERVICE WITH ALL HEART
description:
**Colossians 3:23-24 _Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for men. Knowing that ye shall receive of the Lord the reward of your inheritance, because ye serve the Lord Christ._**

Every work that we do (daily chores, business, education) should be done wholeheartedly as if we were doing it for the Lord, not for the love of men or for namesake. When he sees us working for Him, he promises us an everlasting reward.

• Our Motivation must be to act with the sense that we are serving the Lord Christ, even if we are not appreciated by men or authorities who depend on us.  
• It should be heartfelt work should not half-heartedly.  
• Reward from God will be better than the appreciation by humans.

_Whatever you do_ - there are works that are so small and insignificant, that doesn't attract praise for anyone, because they are never noticed by others. There are several small actions that others do as little as arranging chairs, switching on fans, cleaning after a meal, ushering others or even smiling and greeting others. Every little act can be done with the right heart and attitude, only then Christ sees it.

It's amazing anyone can honor God and bring a smile on His face by small acts of love shown to others.

**Practical action:  
**Find a small thing you can do for the church or for a friend or stranger with the heart of Jesus.

title: Day 14: GOD WILL NOT FORGET YOUR SERVICE
description:
**Hebrews 6:10** **_<sup>10</sup> God is not unjust; he will not forget your work and the love you have shown him as you have helped his people and continue to help them._**

God is not unjust and will not unjustly turn away true believers. He is a faithful God to his followers. God sees our acts of love, help we lend to others, hours you spend to encourage others, take accusations when it's not your fault. No matter how badly you may have been treated by others, God is faithful, he sees your faithfulness, he sees your trust in him and never forgets to lift you in your time of need.

What you do to others will be done back to you. The measure you use will be used for you. Every suffering will be blessed with joy or even profit. God is for us, He is with us and not against us. As a Christian we pushed aside, and looked upon without kindness, God will reward you and carry you through the skies when the wicked will watch your name called out aloud. Don't stop doing good to others.

**Practical Actions:**

Pray for your salvation. May our Lord look at us with his kindness today.

title: Day 15: ENCOURAGE AND BUILD UP
description:
** **1 Thessalonians 5:11, 15 11 "Therefore encourage one another and build one another up, just as in fact you are doing. " 15 "See that no one repays anyone evil for evil, but always seek to do good to one another and to everyone. "**
These verses are excellent guidelines for building a healthy, loving Christian community. **Building One Another (v. 11) **We can Encourage weary believers with words and deeds that can lift them up. You could be a support and not an obstacle to the spiritual growth of others. We can comfort those who are defeated, failed, depressed and weak. **Repay with Good (v. 15) **If anyone does evil to us, we must not do evil to them in return. We must always do good, not only to those in your church but also to all people in the world. We get hurt, we get mocked, we get pushed around at work. We don't want others to take advantage of us so we push back, pay back, speak back. We cannot change this world if we behave like this world. Instead encourage, build up others, pay back evil with good actions and respond with gentleness and kindness.
**Practical Actions: **Today when you are pressed to react, pray to respond in a good way. When you do that today, be proud of yourself for choosing to do good. Do not react but respond.

title: Day 16: BE DEVOTED IN DOING GOOD
description:
**Titus 3:8** **_This is a trustworthy saying. And I want you to stress these things, so that those who have trusted in God may be careful to devote themselves to doing what is good. These things are excellent and profitable for everyone._**

The verse teaches us that since we trusted in God, we have to devote ourselves in doing good. To devote is to make it a habit to consistently practice a new thing.

Salvation is not of our works, but of the grace of God. But those who have experienced that grace must live a life flourishing in good works to others.  
Every good deed we do reveals the love of Christ to others. Comforting, helping, caring for the poor, praying for the sick, and comforting the brokenhearted are good works pleasing to God.

Faith should be expressed not only in words but also in deeds. Then our life will be a blessing to others and bring glory to God. Let us express the love of Christ to everyone we meet today.

**Practical Actions:  
**Have courage to devote yourself to a new habit of doing good to others. Pray for that habit today, soon it will grow in you.

title: Day 17: SERVE WITHOUT ANY CONDITION
description:
**Luke 6:35 "But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them without expecting to get anything back. Then your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High, because he is kind to the ungrateful and wicked."**

Jesus doesn't just ask us to serve people who are easy to love. He's talking to a crowd that understood "love your neighbour" and have never heard a teaching -"love your enemy." **The call is to "do good" with no strings attached.** _"Do good to them, and lend them without expecting to get anything back."_

Most of the time we serve people who can serve us back like friends, family, co-workers. Jesus pushes us past that circle.

**True service is:**

- Helping the co-worker who never helps you
- Making time for the neighbour who's hard to love
- Giving your energy to someone who can't repay you
- Serving one another starts when we release our right to be paid back.

**The motive is that We resemble our Father**

V35"..._because he is kind to the ungrateful and wicked."_

God showed kindness to us when we were ungrateful and He stil does. Remember: you are imitating the character of the Most High. As His offspring you are to imitate Him. In other words, when you give grace freely, You look most like your Father.

**The promise is your reward that will be great**

The reward isn't always public applause or instant payback. It's the deep joy of partnership with God, freedom from bitterness, and the kind of character that lasts into eternity.

**Practical Actions:**

If there is an enemy or person you deeply have dislike, pray for that person to be forgiven.

title: Day 18: SACRIFICAL SERVICE
description:
**_Romans 12:1_** **"_Therefore, I urge you, brothers and sisters, in view of God's mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God-this is your true and proper worship."_**

**God's Mercy is the Foundation, "Therefore"**

Paul's word **"Therefore"** marks a turning point-from deep theology (Romans 1-11) to practical living. It stands on the foundation of **God's mercy**. Mercy is not just a feeling-it acts. Jesus touched lepers, ate with sinners, wept at Lazarus' tomb, died on the cross, and rose again. When our response to mercy is **surrender** instead of fear then, Worship becomes **gratitude**, not performance.

**Living Sacrifice is Daily Surrender**

A living sacrifice means a **lifestyle of surrender**-daily obedience, humility, purity, forgiveness, and generosity. **Examples:** Abraham offering Isaac (surrendering the dearest) "**_God himself will provide_**", Jesus in Gethsemane saying, _"_**_Not my will, but Yours be done._**_"_ Galatians 2:20 - _"_**_I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me_**_."_

**True Worship is Transformation, Not Performance**

**Holy and Pleasing to God -** Worship is not songs or ceremonies-it's a lifestyle. It displays integrity at work, kindness in conflict, forgiveness when it hurts, purity in temptation, generosity in giving, prayer in faith, and service in humility.

**Practical Action:**

Pray to God today to help you to be sacrificial, maybe plan a day of fast, maybe offer food to someone or help a poor person if you see one.

title: Day 19: THOSE WHO ARE FIRST SHOULD SERVE
description:
**

**Mark 10-42-45** **<sup>42</sup> Jesus called them together and said, "You know that those who are regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their high officials exercise authority over them. <sup>43</sup> Not so with you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, <sup>44</sup> and whoever wants to be first must be slave of all. <sup>45</sup> For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."**

In the kingdom of the world, the power is given to suppress people, to make one think superior, but in the kingdom of God we are chosen and given power to serve.

Every one of us a is leader in someplace either at home as husband or parents or elder sibling, or even at workplace. When we are in a position of leadership, we are chosen by God to serve those under us in humility not authority.

If any of us are fortunate to mentor someone in your ministry, it's a great chance to serve them and not consider yourself a master over them.

It's a blessing that God has picked us from this world to serve than to be served. Jesus too became a leader to serve.

There is no such thing as "greatness" in God's Kingdom, we are all equal.

We must imitate Jesus' sacrifice in serving and loving others. If you have learnt or exercised authority wrongly, reflect on Jesus's request to learn a lesson on being a servant.

**Practical Actions:**  
**Is there someone you treated unfairly, can your pray for them today. Are you courageous to apologise to them?**

title: Day 20: THE SERVANT KING
description:
*John 13:12-14 <sup>[12]</sup> When he had finished washing their feet, he put on his clothes and returned to his place. "Do you understand what I have done for you?" he asked them. <sup>[13]</sup> "You call me 'Teacher' and 'Lord,' and rightly so, for that is what I am. <sup>[14]</sup> Now that I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another's feet.*

When Jesus finished washing His disciples' feet, He asked, "Do you understand what I have done for you?" The Son of God, the Creator of heaven and earth, stooped down to perform the task of a servant. In that moment, He redefined greatness - not as power or prestige, but as humility expressed through love.

Jesus' act was not symbolic alone; it was prophetic. He showed that the path to the cross is paved with service. The basin and towel became instruments of grace, revealing that divine authority flows through compassion. When He said, "You call me Teacher and Lord, and rightly so," that's His identity - yet He used his position to lift others.

Are we willing to serve when no one notices? Can we love someone when it costs our pride? True discipleship begins at the feet of others, where love kneels and grace flows. Seek opportunities to serve quietly. Leading is not standing tall but influencing through compassion.

**Practical Actions:**

Let us imitate the heart of Christ in our leadership. In our leadership, let our hearts be ready to kneel before others. Make a shift from Leading to Serving and Leaders to Servants.

title: Day 21: SERVE GOD WITH A GRATEFUL HEART
description:
**

As Samuel gave his final counsel to Israel, he urged them to remain faithful to God than to people. Though they had asked for a king, their greatest responsibility was still to fear the Lord and serve Him with all their hearts.

The fear of the Lord is not a fear that drives us away from God, but a deep reverence and respect that draws us closer to Him. It is recognizing His holiness, honoring His authority, and choosing to obey His will. As **Psalm 111:10** teaches, **"The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom."** When we truly respect God, we gain wisdom to live according to His ways and avoid the paths that lead us away from Him.

Samuel also reminded the people to consider the great things God had done for them. We often forget God's blessings and faithfulness. But when we reflect on how He has guided, protected, and provided for us, our hearts are filled with gratitude and trust. Remembering God's goodness strengthens our faith and motivates us to serve Him wholeheartedly.

Today, take a moment to recall God's faithfulness in your life. Let a reverent fear of the Lord inspire you to serve Him faithfully with all your heart.

**Practical Actions:**  
In your prayer today, Promise to God that he will always be your Only LORD, that you will never turn to anyone or anything else that will turn your heart.

title: Day 22: SERVE THE LEAST AMONG YOU
description:
**Matthew 25:35-40 "<sup>35</sup> For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you invited me in, <sup>36</sup> I needed clothes and you clothed me, I was sick and you looked after me, I was in prison and you came to visit me.'<sup>37</sup> "Then the righteous will answer him, 'Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink? <sup>38</sup> When did we see you a stranger and invite you in, or needing clothes and clothe you? <sup>39</sup> When did we see you sick or in prison and go to visit you? <sup>40</sup> "The King will reply, 'Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me."**

In this passage, Jesus teaches that every act of kindness shown to others is considered service to Him. When we help those in need, encourage the discouraged, or care for our brothers and sisters, we are ministering to Christ Himself.

At times, we may hesitate to help others because of personal feelings, disagreements, or judgments. We may think they do not deserve our help or that their problems are not our responsibility. Yet Jesus calls us to look beyond these attitudes and serve with love and compassion.

It is often easy to help those who can benefit us or those in positions of influence. However, Jesus highlights the importance of serving the humble, weak, and overlooked. Our willingness to care for those who cannot repay us reveals the humility and sincerity of our hearts.

God does not overlook even the smallest act of service. What we do for others, especially those in need, and the least, we do for Jesus. As His followers, we are called to reflect His love by serving others wholeheartedly and selflessly.

**Practical Actions:**  
Today remember to pray to God to teach you help others. Pray for someone whom you know is in great need financially or a better job, etc.

title: Day 23: SHINE THROUGH YOUR GOOD DEEDS
description:
**Matthew 5:16 _Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven._**

Everyone sees you SHINE when you do good deeds to others. When we live according to Gods Word, we want others to see in us the qualities of love, mercy, justice, righteousness, and compassion that help others.

We need to consider how we can do good things for others who live near you, we need to consider our actions to glorify the Father.To what extent have we demonstrated Gods love by doing good things in the lives of others? Now let us repent and be a light in the lives of many, showing goodness in the times of afflictions of others.

Doing good to others is a conscious action that we need to learn to do. It is not natural to be helpful, but we must consciously remind ourselves to be eager to serve when there is an opportunity.

**Practical Actions:**

Today be intentional to jump in to help someone when they are in need. Pray for it and be ready to respond.

title: Day 24: DON'T LOOSE YOUR HEART TO SERVE
description:
** **Romans 12:9-13 9 Love must be sincere. Hate what is evil; cling to what is good. 10 Be devoted to one another in love. Honor one another above yourselves. 11 Never be lacking in zeal, but keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord. 12 Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, faithful in prayer. 13 Share with the Lord's people who are in need. Practice hospitality.** Paul sums up how our character, love, and relationships with others should change after we accept Christ. Hate the bad in the world and love the good. Be completely devoted to each other, not only on Sundays. Find ways to honor each other, lift them, encourage those who are humble and in low positions financially.
There is no room for complacency. There should be no laziness that should hold us back for serving others. Your old age should not cause you to slow down or sit back from responsibility. Find joy in the hope of salvation daily. Pray for yourself, your dear ones, members, relatives, colleges, friends and people you know. Your prayer can do more than your actions to all of them
**Practical Actions:** **Make a prayer list of all the people you know. Hard but give some time to make the list and pray.**

title: Day 25: SERVING WITH A HUMBLE HEART
description:
**1 Peter 5:5 "_And all of you must clothe yourselves with humility in your dealings with one another, for 'God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble."_**

Peter wrote these words to believers who were facing difficulties and pressures from the world around them. In such circumstances, it is easy to become self-focused, seeking recognition, control, or personal advantage. Yet Peter calls Christians to put on humility as though it were a garment. Humility is not merely an attitude; it is a daily choice that shapes how we treat others.

Peter supports this command with a powerful truth: "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble." The proud person relies on personal strength and achievement, while the humble person depends upon God. Pride creates distance from God because it promotes self-sufficiency. Humility opens the heart to receive God's grace, guidance, and strength.

In a culture that often celebrates self-promotion and personal success, this verse reminds us that God's values are different. True spiritual strength is not found in exalting ourselves but in submitting ourselves to God and serving others with a humble heart.

**Practical Actions:**

Pray for the pride in your personal life. Ask God to teach you humility with people you fail to show humility.

title: Day 26: REVEAL YOUR GREATNESS THROUGH SERVICE
description:
**John 13:12-14 "<sup>12</sup> When he had finished washing their feet, he put on his clothes and returned to his place. "Do you understand what I have done for you?" he asked them. <sup>13</sup> "You call me 'Teacher' and 'Lord,' and rightly so, for that is what I am. <sup>14</sup> Now that I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another's feet."**

When we read this passage, we often focus on humility and service, and rightly so. Yet Jesus is teaching something more, that is **obedience.** After giving His disciples an example to follow, He called them to do as He had done. The lesson was not simply to admire His actions but to imitate them through obedience.

True obedience is willing, joyful, and complete. It follows Christ even when His commands are difficult, uncomfortable, or contrary to our natural preferences. Obedience is not choosing only the commands we like; it is surrendering our will to His.

One of the clearest expressions of obedience is serving others. Jesus served not only those who were loyal and loving but also those who would misunderstand, abandon, betray, and deny Him. In the same way, God calls us to serve people who may be difficult, ungrateful, or even hurtful. We put their needs before our own, not because they deserve it, but because we desire to obey Christ and follow His example.

As disciples, we serve others not merely out of duty, but as an act of obedience to our Lord. When we imitate Christ's heart of service, we demonstrate that we truly belong to Him.

**Practical Actions:**

Today, do one act of obedience to Christ to serve someone lesser than you.

title: Day 27: LIVE WITH HUMILITY AND UNITY
description:
**Romans 12:16** **Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but be willing to associate with people of low position. Do not be conceited.**

As believers, we must love one another and live in unity. Instead of boasting about our knowledge, position, or wealth, we should humbly respect others. Living in harmony means everyone singing in the same tune for a song; if we are not in harmony then each one will sing in different tone which sounds like a noise not song. In harmony means being different individuals but being like-minded and united in our motives.

Jesus Christ demonstrated true humility throughout His life. Humility is not merely having a low opinion of oneself; it is willingly choosing the lowly place for the sake of others and in obedience to God. Though He was Lord of all, Jesus humbled Himself and entered this world as a human being, growing up in a humble family. He submitted Himself to baptism by John, served others selflessly, endured rejection and suffering, and ultimately died on a cross among criminals.

Consider the contrast: the King of heaven left the glory of heaven, where He was worshiped by angels, and came to earth to experience hardship, humiliation, and pain. He allowed Himself to be mocked, beaten, and crucified by those He came to save. What greater example of humility could there be? Jesus willingly laid aside His rights and privileges so that God's purpose could be fulfilled and humanity could be redeemed.

Let us examine our lives today. If there is any pride, arrogance, or a tendency to look down on others, let us confess it to God and pray that He grants us humility and unity to treat people who are not like us with respect and goodness.

**Practical Actions:**

If you have avoided anyone in your church as not like you, can you list three people whom you can fellowship and show kindness.

title: Day 28: LIGHT SHINES IN THE DARKNESS
description:
** Matthew 5: 14 - 16 14 "You are the light of the world. A town built on a hill cannot be hidden. 15 Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a bowl. Instead they put it on its stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house. 16 In the same way, let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.** We all know that we need light when we are in the dark. Jesus tells us how we got that light and how we are to use it. We are in the light today because a person has given us the light of God's grace so we found Christ. It does not matter whether we live in the life we have thus received or whether we let others live in Christ's salvation. Are we helping others to receive God's light? Matthew 5:13 - Just as the hilltop city is visible from every angle, so too the grace we have received from God helps us to be visible as followers of Christ. Are we revealing the light of salvation that we have received? To serve others you need to allow your light to shine before others. Only when others see you, they are attracted to the true light, Jesus Christ. Your good actions can draw 100s of people to believe there is God among us who can save.
**Practical Actions:** Make effort today to reveal your light to others by reaching out to someone in the dark. It could be sharing a scripture or your testimony or your transformation to them.

title: Day 29: SERVICE NOT IN WORDS BUT IN ACTION
description:
**James 2:14-17 _14 What good is it, my brothers and sisters, if someone claims to have faith but has no deeds? Can such faith save them? 15 Suppose a brother or a sister is without clothes and daily food. 16 If one of you says to them, "Go in peace; keep warm and well fed," but does nothing about their physical needs, what good is it? 17 In the same way, faith by itself, if it is not accompanied by action, is dead._** The book of James was written for the Jews of that time who believed in Jesus, but they didn't show their faith through actions. James too did not believe in Jesus until his resurrection. Then he teaches that faith alone will not save us, it should show through your actions.
He teaches of an inseparable connection between faith and works. He teaches that if one's faith is genuine, he or she must express faith in good works that meet the needs of others. Throughout this month, we have studied what kind of servants we are called to be, and how our ministry should always be in action, not just in words of mouth. So let us improve our ministry. Share your clothes, make a meal for someone, pay someone's bill if you can, help them get a job, teach someone to save money etc. There are many ways to help others. **Practical Actions:** Text a friend and ask if they need your help today. Or listen to their challenges and pray for a blessing in their life.

title: Day 30: YOU CANNOT SERVE TWO MASTERS
description:
**Matthew 6:24** **"_No one can serve two masters. Either you will hate the one and love the other, or you will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money."_**

Jesus teaches that true service requires wholehearted devotion. We cannot serve God while our hearts are controlled by other desires. A servant belongs to one master, and his loyalty, affection, and obedience are directed toward that master alone. This is why Jesus said, "You cannot serve both God and money."

Many Christians struggle in this area. They may have followed Christ for many years and remained faithful through many challenges, yet still find themselves divided between two masters. The pull of comfort, success, possessions, approval, or personal ambition can slowly compete for the place that belongs to God alone. A divided heart weakens our devotion to Christ and hinders our spiritual growth.

Understanding what it means to serve one Master is essential for every disciple. We must continually examine our hearts and ask whether God truly has first place in our lives.

Helping others understand this truth is also an important service to God. Not all service is practical or visible. Teaching, encouraging, correcting, and strengthening others in their faith are valuable acts of service. Many disciples drift away not because they reject God outright, but because their hearts gradually become attached to other masters. They need loving guidance and biblical teaching to help them return to wholehearted devotion.

**Practical Action**

If you are mentoring or discipling someone, take time this week to teach them about serving one Master. Right teaching can rescue a drifting soul, strengthen faith, and draw hearts back to God. When we help others remain devoted to Christ, we are serving both them and the Lord.

title: Day 31: TWO IMPORTANT TRUTHS
description:
**Galatians 5:13-15** **_<sup>"</sup>You, my brothers and sisters, were called to be free. But do not use your freedom to indulge the flesh; rather, serve one another humbly in love. For the entire law is fulfilled in keeping this one command: "Love your neighbor as yourself." If you bite and devour each other, watch out or you will be destroyed by each other"_**

As we conclude this month's meditation on service, Paul leaves us with two important truths. First, serving one another in love fulfills God's law. Second, biting and devouring one another will ultimately destroy us.

Christian freedom is not meant to be used for selfish desires. Instead, God calls us to use our freedom to serve others humbly in love. This is not according to our own standard of love or humility, but according to the example of Jesus Christ. He loved the unlovable, served those who failed Him, and put the needs of others before His own. As followers of Christ, we are called to imitate that same love and humility.

Paul also gives a strong warning. When we criticize, tear down, mislead, or become a stumbling block to others, we are not serving Christ. Instead of building up the body of Christ, we contribute to its harm. We must be careful so that our words and actions must strengthen people's faith rather than weaken it.

Let us choose to serve rather than tear down, encourage rather than discourage, and build up rather than destroy, lead through scriptures rather than misleading through your own knowledge. When we serve others with the love of Christ, we fulfill God's command and bring glory to Him.

**Prayer:**

Father, help me to serve others with the love and humility of Jesus. Guard my words and actions so that I build others up and never become a cause for their stumbling. May my life reflect Your love and bring encouragement to those around me. Amen.
